description: agent-symbiont fleet: self-evolving binaries reporting evolution pipeline health, LLM token consumption, revision registry state and the trading performance of the code the LLM just wrote. Designed for many concurrent instances -- filter via the model/instance variables; all timeseries break down per instance. Events arrive in bursts (a refinement round every ~2-3 min), so all rates/ratios/means use fixed 30m windows -- short windows render as unreadable combs and zero-valued stats. The Training harness / Pareto frontier / Last evaluated candidate / Persistence rows cover the agent_symbiont_* series emitted by the agent-symbiont harness on top of the framework. NOTE: neither exporter configures histogram bucket bounds, so every histogram is exported as a summary whose quantile series only hold the exporter's 60s rolling window and read 0 in between, while _sum/_count stay cumulative -- hence means are derived from rate(_sum)/rate(_count) and the quantile panels filter != 0 and span the gaps. The LLM context budget row sizes the vLLM context window against actual prompt sizes; its 131072-token reference is hardcoded in those queries and thresholds, so update it there when the server setting changes. The two payload panels in that row need symbiont >= 0.23.0, which measures the serialized body of every outbound request; they read No data against older agents.
title: symbiont

panels.description: Number of symbiont instances currently reporting metrics (matching the model/instance filters).
panels.title: Instances

panels.description: Completed agentic LLM runs per hour across the selected fleet, smoothed over a 30-minute window.
panels.title: LLM runs / h

panels.description: Fraction of evolution attempts that produced an activated revision (activations / attempts). The complement is the failure ratio (parse / compile / signature / no_rust_code).
panels.title: Attempt success ratio

panels.description: Failed evolution attempts per hour across the fleet (all failure kinds).
panels.title: Evolve failures / h

panels.description: Mean wall-clock duration of Runtime::evolve calls (including retries), derived from the summary _sum/_count.
panels.title: Mean evolve duration

panels.description: LLM output tokens produced by the selected fleet over the last 24h (increase over a fixed 24h window, robust to process restarts / counter resets).
panels.title: Output tokens (24h)

panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time the single build slot is occupied, for the worst instance. `Runtime::build_and_register` serializes compile+load behind one `Mutex` over one shared crate directory, so the sum of compile and load seconds observed per second of wall clock IS that slot's utilization -- it cannot exceed 1 per process. Once it approaches 1 no amount of extra inference concurrency buys throughput: every additional lane just queues on `cargo` (visible as a rising symbiont_build_slot_wait_seconds), and `symbiont_inference_in_flight` sags below the limit because lanes are stuck in the local stage instead of talking to the endpoint. Green <60%, yellow 60-85%, red >85%. This tile is the verdict; the tile to its right is the raw number.
panels.title: Compile bottleneck?

panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time the single build slot is occupied, for the worst instance. `Runtime::build_and_register` serializes compile+load behind one `Mutex` over one shared crate directory, so the sum of compile and load seconds observed per second of wall clock IS that slot's utilization -- it cannot exceed 1 per process. Once it approaches 1 no amount of extra inference concurrency buys throughput: every additional lane just queues on `cargo` (visible as a rising symbiont_build_slot_wait_seconds), and `symbiont_inference_in_flight` sags below the limit because lanes are stuck in the local stage instead of talking to the endpoint. Green <60%, yellow 60-85%, red >85%.
panels.title: Build slot utilization (worst instance)

panels.description: Mean concurrent inference requests over the limit (`Runtime::max_in_flight`), averaged over 30m. The InferenceGate meters HTTP requests rather than lanes, so this should sit near 100% for as long as there is work queued: every point below it is an unfilled slot in the server's continuous batch, and decode throughput scales with that batch. Persistently low here while the build slot tile is red means the harness is compile-bound, not endpoint-bound. No value = no limit configured (unlimited gate reports capacity 0).
panels.title: Inference saturation

panels.description: Failed evolution attempts per hour by failure kind (parse / compile / signature / no_rust_code), summed across selected instances. Compile failures dominating suggests prompt or crate-context issues.
panels.title: Evolve failures / h by kind

panels.description: Revision activations per hour per instance -- the fleet's effective evolution throughput.
panels.title: Revision activations / h by instance

panels.description: Mean attempts per Runtime::evolve call per instance (1 = first-try success). Rising values mean the model needs more retries to produce loadable code.
panels.title: Mean attempts per evolve by instance

panels.description: Mean duration per evolution pipeline stage (llm / parse_validate / compile / load), derived from summary _sum/_count. Log scale: llm dominates by orders of magnitude.
panels.title: Mean stage duration

panels.description: Mean wall-clock Runtime::evolve duration (including retries) per instance. Slow instances point at contended LLM backends or slow compile hosts.
panels.title: Mean evolve duration by instance

panels.description: Concurrent inference requests the gate admits, per instance (`Runtime::set_max_in_flight`). 0 / no value means the gate is unlimited and the provider does the admission control.
panels.title: Slot limit (max_in_flight)

panels.description: Mean inference requests resident at the endpoint. Compare against the slot limit to the left.
panels.title: In-flight (mean 30m)

panels.description: Slot limit minus mean in-flight: inference concurrency the harness is paying for and not using. Non-zero while lanes remain means the lanes are stuck in a local stage (compile / load / parse), not waiting on the model.
panels.title: Idle slots (mean 30m)

panels.description: Mean requests waiting at the gate. Queued > 0 with in-flight at the limit is the healthy, saturated state: the endpoint is the bottleneck. Queued == 0 with in-flight *below* the limit is the compile-bound state.
panels.title: Queued for a slot (mean 30m)

panels.description: Mean seconds a request waited for a gate slot, over all requests (a zero is recorded for every request admitted immediately, so this is diluted by design -- it answers 'how hard is the limit binding', not 'how long do blocked requests wait').
panels.title: Mean slot wait

panels.description: Mean seconds a lane waited for the build `Mutex` before it could compile. This is the direct cost of serializing builds against one shared crate directory. It should stay near zero while inference dominates; if it grows to the order of the mean compile time, `cargo` is the limiter.
panels.title: Mean build slot wait

panels.description: The saturation picture per instance. The limit is a step function set by `Runtime::set_max_in_flight` (evolve_batch* sets it per call); in-flight should ride along it while work remains, with queued absorbing the excess. In-flight dipping away from the limit while queued is flat at 0 is the signature of the local stages (compile/load) starving the endpoint.
panels.title: Inference slots: limit vs in-flight vs queued

panels.description: How long requests sit at the gate before reaching the endpoint. `mean` is over all requests (zeros included); `p99` is the exporter's rolling-60s 99th percentile, i.e. the tail actually paid by blocked requests. The gate serves higher attempt numbers first, so repairs should show a shorter tail than fresh work -- if p99 climbs without the limit changing, the endpoint slowed down.
panels.title: Inference slot wait

panels.description: Fraction of wall-clock time the single build slot is occupied, for the worst instance. `Runtime::build_and_register` serializes compile+load behind one `Mutex` over one shared crate directory, so the sum of compile and load seconds observed per second of wall clock IS that slot's utilization -- it cannot exceed 1 per process. Once it approaches 1 no amount of extra inference concurrency buys throughput: every additional lane just queues on `cargo` (visible as a rising symbiont_build_slot_wait_seconds), and `symbiont_inference_in_flight` sags below the limit because lanes are stuck in the local stage instead of talking to the endpoint. Green <60%, yellow 60-85%, red >85%. The dashed threshold band marks 85%: above it, raising `max_in_flight` cannot help and the fix is to remove the serialization (a pool of crate directories keyed by revision id, with the dedup map moved outside the build lock).
panels.title: Build slot utilization by instance

panels.description: Mean seconds per attempt for the two stages that matter, plus the two queue waits, on a log scale. The bottleneck rule of thumb: the build slot binds once `compile >= llm / max_in_flight`, because that is the point at which one serialized compile takes longer than the interval between completions of `max_in_flight` concurrent generations. `llm / limit` is plotted directly as that break-even line -- when `compile` crosses above it, the harness is compile-bound.
panels.title: Where lane time goes: llm vs compile vs queues

panels.description: Token consumption per second by kind (input / cached_input / output), summed across selected instances, smoothed over 30m. cached_input is cheap; watch fresh input + output for cost.
panels.title: Token rate by kind

panels.description: Total token consumption per second per instance (all kinds). Identifies which fleet members burn the most LLM capacity.
panels.title: Token rate by instance

panels.description: Mean tokens and messages per agentic run (fleet-wide, from summary _sum/_count). Growing input tokens per run = context bloat in the evolution prompts.
panels.title: Mean tokens & messages per run

panels.description: Completed agentic runs per hour by outcome, plus transient LLM retries per hour. Anything other than `ok` deserves a look at the logs; rising retries point at a flaky LLM backend.
panels.title: LLM runs / h by outcome

panels.description: Ratio of inference requests that failed, by failure category: each band is that category's failed runs over all LLM runs, and stacked they sum to the total inference error rate. `context_overflow` and `transient` are the two categories the self-healing loop recovers from; `http` is provider rejections it does not.
panels.title: Inference error ratio by category

panels.description: 99th percentile prompt (input token) size per agentic run over the selected range, to be read against the 128k context window configured on the vLLM service. Derived from the exporter summary series quantile="1" (the max within its 60s rolling window), which is effectively one sample per run because refinement rounds are ~2-3 min apart; the 30s subquery step reads those samples and the != 0 filter drops the idle windows that report 0. Thresholds are 70% / 85% / 95% of the window.
panels.title: P99 prompt size (range)

panels.description: Largest prompt (input tokens) any single run sent in the selected range, per instance. This is the number that must fit in the context window together with the generated reply, so it -- not the mean -- is the hard constraint on the 128k setting. At or above the window, requests were already rejected or silently truncated by the server.
panels.title: Peak prompt size (range)

panels.description: Peak prompt size as a fraction of the 131072-token (128k) context window configured on the vLLM service (hosts/desg0/configuration.nix, maxModelLen). The divisor is hardcoded: update it here whenever that setting changes. >85% leaves no room for the reply plus one retry round of accumulated history; >=100% means the window is the binding limit.
panels.title: Peak context usage vs 128k

panels.description: Times the framework hit the server context limit and recovered by discarding the accumulated retry history and restarting from the base prompt (symbiont_evolve_context_window_resets_total). Any non-zero value is direct proof the window is too small, and it costs quality: the discarded history is the compiler/validation feedback the LLM was self-healing from. The series only starts existing once it fires, hence the 0 while healthy. It counts hard 400s only (exceed_context_size / context_length_exceeded / "prompt is too long"), so a server that silently shifts or truncates the context reports none -- read it together with the peak panels.
panels.title: Context window overflows (range)

panels.description: Distribution of prompt sizes (input tokens per agentic run) over the selected range, bucketed in 4096-token steps, combined across the selected instances. Sampled from the quantile="1" summary series, so each run contributes the scrapes of its own 60s window (~12 at the 5s scrape interval) and the shape is per-run weighted. Judge the right tail against the 128k window: a tail already reaching ~110k means the next prompt-growing change (larger pareto frontier render, longer retry history, bigger generated source) overflows it.
panels.title: Prompt size distribution (input tokens per run)

panels.description: Prompt size per run over time against the 128k context window (dashed red threshold line). "peak input" is the per-run input tokens (quantile="1" summary series, zeros filtered, gaps spanned); "mean input" is rate(_sum)/rate(_count) over 30m; "peak input + output" adds the generated reply, which occupies the same window on the server, so it approximates the real per-run context footprint -- approximates, because both maxima are per 60s window and can come from two different runs when several land in one window. A rising trend is prompt bloat (retry history, frontier cards, source size) rather than a one-off outlier. Values are provider-reported usage aggregated over a run's turns.
panels.title: Prompt size per run vs context window

panels.description: Serialized size of the request bodies actually sent to the inference endpoint (symbiont_llm_request_body_bytes, symbiont >= 0.23.0). This is the exact payload -- system preamble including the rendered crate docs, accumulated chat history, tool definitions and the new turn -- measured per HTTP request rather than per agentic run, so every tool-calling turn and every retry is its own sample, and it is recorded before the server answers, so requests the endpoint rejects as too large are counted here while they are missing from the token metrics. "peak payload" is the quantile="1" summary series (zeros filtered, gaps spanned), "mean payload" is rate(_sum)/rate(_count) over 30m. Convert to tokens with the bytes-per-token panel on the right.
panels.title: Request payload size per request

panels.description: Two ratios that make the payload and token metrics comparable (symbiont >= 0.23.0). "bytes per input token" = rate(symbiont_llm_request_body_bytes_sum) / rate(symbiont_llm_run_input_tokens_sum): the measured JSON-bytes-per-token of the deployed tokenizer (expect ~3-4 for English prose and Rust), which converts the payload panel on the left into the token units the context window is enforced in. "requests per run" = rate(symbiont_llm_request_body_bytes_count) / rate(symbiont_llm_runs_total{outcome="ok"}): a value above 1 means an agentic run issues several HTTP requests (tool turns, rig retries) and its reported usage is the sum over them -- in that case the per-run token panels overstate the size of any single request, and only the payload panel is a true per-request measurement.
panels.title: Payload calibration: bytes per token & requests per run

panels.description: Revisions retained in the keep-all registry per instance. Grows monotonically; watch alongside dylib size for disk usage (~49 MB per dylib observed).
panels.title: Revisions loaded & active id by instance

panels.description: Mean generated Rust source size and compiled dylib size per revision (fleet-wide, from summary _sum/_count). Log scale: dylibs are ~4 orders of magnitude larger than their source.
panels.title: Mean artifact size per revision

panels.description: Backtest throughput across selected instances, summed over splits (train/test). Includes both freshly evolved candidates and the re-evaluation of retained frontier candidates against the slid dataset window; the harness no longer labels the two apart.
panels.title: Backtests / s

panels.description: Fraction of backtests aborted early because the evolved code panicked. A rising ratio means the LLM generates crashier code.
panels.title: Backtest panic ratio

panels.description: Completed refinement rounds per hour (evolve + evaluate + persist), all outcomes.
panels.title: Rounds / h

panels.description: Fraction of refinement rounds that completed (outcome ok); the complement aborted the training run on a failed evolution.
panels.title: Round success ratio

panels.description: Time since the most recent successfully completed training run. Training runs daily; alert past ~26h.
panels.title: Since last successful train

panels.description: Backtest throughput broken down by dataset split (train/test). rate() of a counter, robust across process restarts. Fresh candidates and frontier re-evaluations share these series; a run with a full frontier spends its first pass re-scoring incumbents.
panels.title: Backtests / s by split

panels.description: Backtests aborted early by a panic in the evolved code, per hour. Should be near zero; spikes correlate with prompt or prelude changes.
panels.title: Backtest panics / h by split

panels.description: Mean wall-clock duration of one evaluation pass (all datasets x all matrix configurations), derived from _sum/_count rates.
panels.title: Mean evaluation duration by split

panels.description: Mean wall-clock duration of one full refinement round (evolve + train/test evaluation + persistence). The evolve share alone is symbiont_evolve_duration_seconds.
panels.title: Mean round duration by instance

panels.description: Refinement rounds per hour by outcome (ok / evolve_failed), 30m smoothed. Counted by the trainer, one increment per round: a round is evolve_failed when every lane of it failed to evolve, so this stays a rate of rounds however many candidates a structure proposes per round.
panels.title: Rounds / h by outcome

panels.description: PARETO ONLY (population=pareto): frontier submissions per hour by verdict. The entered share is the headline signal that the agentic loop still produces improving candidates. NOTE: this counts re-submissions of retained incumbents (re-scored on the slid dataset window, where entered means the incumbent survived the slide) in the SAME series as freshly evolved candidates, so a run starting with a full frontier adds one submission per incumbent before its first round. Treat this as a per-submission funnel, not a per-proposal success rate; the per-round breakdown lives in ClickHouse.
panels.title: Frontier verdicts / h by verdict

panels.description: Population decisions per hour, by population structure and by that structure's own name for the decision (30m smoothed). Stacked, so the height is the decision throughput and the composition is the admission funnel. The outcome vocabulary is deliberately per-structure - a pareto frontier says entered/dominated, a (mu + lambda) population says survived/truncated - and the harness only stores it; the one bit it interprets is the retained label plotted beside this. Counts window-slide re-submissions of retained incumbents alongside fresh proposals.
panels.title: Population outcomes / h by outcome

panels.description: Share of a population's decisions that kept the candidate, by structure. Computed from the retained label rather than from an enumeration of outcome names, so it keeps working for a structure that invents a new word for keeping something. A run that starts with a full population drags this up before its first round (every incumbent is re-submitted and survives the window slide), so read it together with the throughput panel, not on its own.
panels.title: Retention rate by population

panels.description: Quality-gate criteria violated by evaluated candidates, per hour by criterion (30m smoothed). Only liquidation and invalid_metrics (SAFETY) reject a candidate; the rest are advisory feedback. The dominating criterion is the gate to tune or the defect the agent must engineer away.
panels.title: Quality gate failures / h by criterion

options.content:
The `agent_symbiont_last_eval_*` series were removed. They claimed to profile "the most recently evaluated candidate", which stops being well defined as soon as a population proposes more than one candidate per round.

Per-candidate objectives, quality gate and population verdict now live in the ClickHouse table `agent_symbiont_evaluations` — one row per candidate per split, keyed by run, round and candidate. Query it there rather than re-adding gauges: it can say *which* candidate and *in which round*, and it is not bounded by a scrape window.

Everything on this dashboard describes the training **process**: throughput, admission rates, durations, persistence health.

panels.title: Per-candidate results live in ClickHouse, not in Prometheus

panels.description: Mean ClickHouse insert latency by store (backtest results, generated candidates, evolve failures), derived from _sum/_count rates.
panels.title: Mean insert duration by store

panels.description: Failed ClickHouse inserts per hour by store. Any non-zero rate stalls or aborts training runs.
panels.title: Insert failures / h by store
